initial.name: anton_restart
initial.description: Restart the agent runtime service so freshly deployed code takes effect. Call this ONLY after a build/deploy step completed (e.g. a plugin or bundle was rebuilt), never mid-task: it terminates this very process, so the CURRENT turn ends immediately and the user starts a new conversation on the restarted app. Do not call it speculatively or more than once per deployment.

initial.name: anton_start
initial.description: Start the agent runtime service if it is stopped, reporting what it did. When everything already runs, it reports that nothing needed starting — safe to call speculatively while diagnosing.

initial.name: anton_status
initial.description: Report the health of the Anton application services: the supervisor bridge, the agent runtime process (with PID and port), and the c0ntext memory engine. Use this to diagnose whether a service is down before attempting anton_start or anton_restart.

initial.name: anton_stop
initial.description: Shut down the agent runtime service. WARNING: you ARE that process — calling this ends your current turn and conversation immediately, and the user brings the app back from its control surface. Call it ONLY when the user explicitly asks to stop or quit the application, never mid-task.

initial.name: bash
initial.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Managed `$DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. An unset variable expands to an empty string, so guard variables in such paths with `${VAR:?}`. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap; on expiry the command moves to the background as a job instead of being killed.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact command the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

initial.name: create_goal
initial.description: Create a persisted goal that keeps this session working across automatic continuation rounds. Use it when the direct human request is a long-running objective, even if the user did not say "goal"; not for single-turn work.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

initial.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

Declare typed ports (inputs/outputs: {name, type: any|string|number|json}) and params ({name, type: string|number|boolean|json, required?, default?}).

description.description: One-line description surfaced in search results and the palette.

sourceFlowId.description: The workflow the block was extracted from, when it has one.

initial.name: flow_save
initial.description: Create or update one workflow definition (it appears on the Dag Flow canvas). Node fields: id (unique), kind (input|output|code|llm|agent|shell|http|condition|transform|library), title, blockId (required for kind=library), params (object, default {}; input nodes carry their literal under value), code (for code/condition: a return-body program reading the plain `inputs` and `params` objects), x, y (canvas position numbers, default 0). Edge fields: id (unique), from {nodeId, port}, to {nodeId, port} — each target port accepts at most one edge, and the graph must stay acyclic. The graph is validated before anything is written; a rejected save writes nothing.

id.description: Existing definition id to update; omit to create a new workflow.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

nodes.description: Node fields: id (unique), kind (input|output|code|llm|agent|shell|http|condition|transform|library), title, blockId (required for kind=library), params (object, default {}; input nodes carry their literal under value), code (for code/condition: a return-body program reading the plain `inputs` and `params` objects), x, y (canvas position numbers, default 0).

edges.description: Edge fields: id (unique), from {nodeId, port}, to {nodeId, port} — each target port accepts at most one edge, and the graph must stay acyclic.

initial.name: glob
initial.description: Find files, not directories, whose paths match a glob pattern, including hidden and ignored files. Returns up to 100 paths in modification-time order; a larger result keeps the first paths and reports where the complete list was saved.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

initial.name: grep
initial.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns up to 250 matches; a larger result reports where the complete match list was saved.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

initial.name: interrupt_agent
initial.description: Ask a subagent to stop its current work. This call returns without waiting for it to stop. You can continue a local direct child's conversation later with send_message. External executions stop permanently and cannot receive follow-ups. Subagents it started will keep running.

agent_id.description: The id of an agent created under you: your direct child or a deeper descendant.

initial.name: job_kill
initial.description: Request cancellation of a running background job.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

initial.name: job_list
initial.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

initial.name: job_output
initial.description: Read a background job: output since the previous read for stream jobs, or the result of a finished final-output job.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job finishes or the timeout expires; a timed-out wait leaves the job running. Defaults to false.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds with wait: true. Defaults to and is capped by configuration.

initial.name: list_agents
initial.description: List subagents you started, with their ids, labels, and status. running means it is working; inactive means it is not currently working. You will be notified when a subagent finishes; there is no need to keep checking its status. Use send_message to continue the conversation. With scope descendants, a child entry may carry `tokens`: its cumulative provider usage, where hit is the cache-read share of its prompt tokens; a high hit means continuing it with send_message is cheaper than starting a fresh agent for related work.

scope.description: children (default) lists direct children, which accept send_message in any status. descendants lists the whole tree below you with each entry's parent session id and depth; entries deeper than 1 accept only interrupt_agent.

initial.name: plan_write
initial.description: Record or update the standing implementation plan for the current work. Use this tool whenever an implementation plan has been produced (e.g. by a planning subagent) or updated. The plan persists across turns and is injected into every subsequent request as a standing guide for both the model and the user. Send the COMPLETE markdown plan, starting with a # heading.

plan.description: The complete implementation plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

title.description: Optional short title for the plan.

path.description: Optional workspace-relative file path to save the plan markdown. Defaults to "implementation_plan.md".

initial.name: read
initial.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

initial.name: read_image
initial.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. Large images are downscaled automatically; do not install image libraries or create thumbnails to inspect an image.

initial.name: send_message
initial.description: Send a message to an agent. A working agent receives it at its next step; an idle agent starts a new turn with it. Returns delivery confirmation, not the agent's answer.

agent_id.description: The agent id of your direct continuable child, or your direct parent when you are a resident continuable child.

message.description: The message to deliver to the agent.

initial.name: set_agent_model
initial.description: Switch a running subagent to another model. Use it when a subagent is stuck because its current model is exhausted, rate-limited, or otherwise unavailable. The change reaches its next model step and is kept if the subagent is later resumed. Only a subagent that is currently loaded can be switched. This changes no queued work; use send_message to give it another task. Prefer a model from the same or a cheaper provider that the subagent can reach.

agent_id.description: The id of an agent created under you: your direct child or a deeper descendant.

provider.description: Provider route of the replacement model, as shown in the available models list.

model.description: Provider-owned model id of the replacement model.

reasoning_effort.description: Optional reasoning effort for the replacement model. Omit to use that model's default.

initial.name: skill
initial.description: Load the full instructions for a skill. Call it before acting on a task that names or clearly matches a skill in the session skill catalog.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

initial.name: subagent
initial.description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. Delegation is the DEFAULT for decomposable work: when a task splits into two or more independent pieces — separate files, surfaces, or concerns — fan them out to parallel subagent calls in one message instead of doing them inline; keep only single-step or strictly sequential actions inline. This tool starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its id. The runtime notifies you when it finishes. The child reports results with `send_message`; use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes. Prefer that continuation over a new child when an existing child already owns the task context.

cwd.description: Initial child working directory. Relative paths use your current directory; omitted inherits it. Later directory changes in either agent are independent.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) durable label naming the domain this child owns (subsystem, surface, or responsibility), not the one-off request. Later tasks match this label to decide whether to continue this child instead of starting a new one.

prompt.description: The complete, self-contained task for the subagent. It does not share this conversation's context, so include everything it needs.

You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its id. The runtime notifies you when it finishes. The child reports results with `send_message`; use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes. Prefer that continuation over a new child when an existing child already owns the task context.

cwd.description: Initial child working directory. Relative paths use your current directory; omitted inherits it. Later directory changes in either agent are independent.

initial.name: todo_write
initial.description:
Create and manage a structured task tree for the current work. Send the ENTIRE tree every call — it REPLACES the previous tree (there are no partial updates, no per-node edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress. Using this tool is the DEFAULT, not an opt-in: before executing any work with more than one step, plan first — recording the plan with plan_write first when the work is non-trivial (3 or more tasks, multi-phase, cross-package, or architectural) — then write the tree and execute against it; do not wait for the user to ask for a plan.

Workflow: plan first, then encode the plan as a todo tree, then execute it one node at a time:

1. Plan: analyze the request and form a step-by-step plan before taking any action. For non-trivial work (3 or more tasks, multi-phase, cross-package, or architectural), record the plan with plan_write BEFORE calling this tool; if a delegating subagent fails or is unavailable, author the plan from current knowledge and proceed inline — never stall on a failed delegation.
2. Write the tree: convert the plan into this tool's `todos` argument. Nest child tasks under a parent when they are its concrete phases or subtasks — up to three levels (task, child, grandchild); never deeper, and keep simple work flat rather than nesting for its own sake.
3. Execute sequentially: keep exactly one branch of work `in_progress`, finish it, mark it `completed`, and move to the next. Update statuses in real time — mark a node completed the moment it is done, never batch completions.

Persistence: the tree OUTLIVES the turn — the user sees it between and across messages, so it is the standing plan, not a per-turn scratchpad. At the start of any new user request that involves multi-step work, plan first (plan_write for non-trivial work), then write the tree (rewriting or extending the standing one) before any other tool call. When later phases or follow-ups remain, leave them `pending` on the tree rather than reporting everything completed; an all-settled tree is only correct when the whole request is genuinely finished.

Delegation: every agent session owns its own tree. As the orchestrator, keep the top-level nodes here; when you delegate one node to a subagent, that node stays on your tree until its subtree reports back, and the subagent tracks its own finer-grained subtree in its own session rather than rewriting yours.

Node fields: `status` is pending (not started) | in_progress (being worked on now) | completed (done) | cancelled (no longer needed); `priority` optionally ranks nodes (high | medium | low). Mark a parent completed only after all of its children are completed or cancelled. Only a trivial single-step request (one obvious action, no phases) may skip the tree; when in doubt, write it.

Parallelism: mark every node being actively worked `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs concurrently (e.g. parallel subagents or background commands); while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`.

todos.description: The COMPLETE task tree, replacing any previous tree. Up to three levels: a top-level task nests children, which may themselves nest grandchildren.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

priority.description: Optional scheduling weight: high | medium | low.

children.description: Subtasks of this node (level two). Each child may itself nest grandchildren (level three); nothing nests below that.

initial.name: workflow
initial.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.
